build_profile: TensorRT 10.3.0 on a Jetson Orin Nano Super (15 W mode, sm_87, CUDA 12.6, JetPack 6). Policy: LeRobot ACT, two ResNet-18 image backbones plus a transformer encoder-decoder (multi-head attention, LayerNorm), 51.6M parameters. INT8 by NVIDIA TensorRT Model Optimizer (modelopt) explicit Q/DQ in PyTorch, ONNX export in an x86 NGC container, engines built on the Orin itself with trtexec --int8 --fp16. Not used: DLA, FP8, GridSample, diffusion models, LLMs, TensorRT-LLM, Torch-TensorRT.

F1.text: On this Orin build, INT8 is slower than FP16: GPU compute 16.8 ms per inference for INT8 against 11.6 ms for FP16 (FP32 53.4 ms), measured with trtexec at batch 1.

F2.text: INT8 uses more energy per inference than FP16: 101 mJ against 82 mJ (FP32 403 mJ), whole-module VDD_IN above idle.

F3.text: Building the INT8 engine with trtexec --int8 alone gave 28.57 ms; with --int8 --fp16 it gave 16.22 ms, because layers without INT8 kernels fell back to FP32 with reformat nodes.

F4.text: modelopt left a quantizer uncalibrated ('Quantizer has not been calibrated') because PyTorch's fused multi-head-attention fast path bypassed the out_proj module; disabling the fast path fixed it.

F5.text: TensorRT engine builds were nondeterministic in latency across rebuilds of the same ONNX; a frozen timing cache made them reproducible.
